title: Fraction line lab
subtitle: Treat each fraction as a position, not only as a pair of numbers.
learning_objective: Locate fractions accurately between whole numbers.

sections.heading: Equal intervals matter
sections.body: To place a fraction, divide the unit interval into equal parts named by the denominator and count parts from zero.

sections.heading: Locate three fourths
sections.caption: The marked point is three of four equal intervals from zero.

steps: Divide the interval into 3 equal spaces.

sections.heading: Position check
sections.body: The point should be beyond one half but before one whole.

title: Fractions between benchmarks
subtitle: Use 0, one half, and 1 as reliable landmarks.

sections.heading: Benchmark first
sections.body: Decide whether a fraction is below, equal to, or above one half before making a finer comparison.

steps: Three eighths is below one half.
Five eighths is above one half.

sections.heading: Same denominator shortcut
sections.body: When pieces are the same size, the larger numerator marks the farther position.

sections.heading: Use distance
sections.body: Describe which benchmark each fraction is closest to.

title: Choose a fraction strategy
subtitle: Read the situation before selecting an operation.
learning_objective: Select addition or subtraction for a fraction situation.

sections.heading: Operation follows meaning
sections.body: Combine parts when quantities join. Find what remains or the difference when a quantity is removed or compared.

sections.problem: A jug held 5/6 litre and 2/6 litre was poured out. What remains?
sections.reasoning: The operation matches the change in the story.

sections.heading: Do not choose by keywords alone
sections.body: Sketch the quantities and decide what changes before calculating.

sections.heading: Check the result
sections.body: A remaining amount must be smaller than the starting amount.

sections.heading: Your turn
sections.prompt: Ravi walked 1/5 km then 3/5 km. Which operation fits?

title: Fraction story lab
subtitle: Represent, solve, and check a multi-step fraction story.
learning_objective: Explain a fraction-operation solution using a representation.

sections.heading: Read, draw, solve, check
steps: Identify the whole and unit fraction.
Check that the result fits the story.

sections.problem: Neha read 2/8 of a book Monday and 3/8 Tuesday. How much altogether?
steps: Both amounts are parts of the same book.

sections.heading: Reasonableness check
sections.body: The answer is below one whole because five of eight equal parts have been read.

sections.heading: Keep the unit visible
sections.body: Write ‘of the book’ so the fraction remains connected to its whole.

sections.heading: Your turn
sections.prompt: If 1/8 more is read, what total is reached?
